claims: The review launcher always creates a new private synthetic realm and uses the existing protected local-password APIs to enroll its generated account, create a neutral Assistant and relationship, and approve independently authored synthetic declarations. It never opens an existing review database. Generated credentials are written only to a mode-0600 file inside a mode-0700 directory, not to command output, URLs, receipts or Git.

The operator session list contains only eligible sessions of the seeded synthetic account with an existing runtime endpoint, omitting revoked, expired and foreign sessions. Numbered selection avoids copying opaque IDs. Setup is an explicit protected configuration draft/activation for the chosen endpoint; it neither changes that session disclosure nor starts capture/output. Profile mutation is rejected and the launcher has a fixed profile loader.

Preparation separately creates one current host-owned check-in, arrival or grounded-follow-up occurrence. The registry binds user, Assistant, relationship, deployment and session; holds at most 128 events; filters expiry; and does not survive host shutdown/restart. No provider call, output-readiness update, consent change or disclosure change occurs during preparation. The follow-up references only the seeded unfinished synthetic exercise. Existing eligibility, cooldown, deduplication and unanswered-topic accounting remain active.

The public guide covers fresh launch, private sign-in, session disclosure, numbered host setup, source preparation and the first-party picker. Fixture and existing ai5090 provider selection are explicit and separate; the launcher does not start provider services, configure tunnels, select another model or fall back. The execution profile remains test and the selected provider profile is recorded separately.

Joined verification exercises a fresh browser sign-in, actual Session disclosure controls, protected synthetic configuration activation, a host-prepared arrival, the labeled picker and adjacent output readiness, and an observed Assistant opening without user input. An API test additionally verifies no-output preparation, missing readiness suppression, grounded follow-up emission, session isolation, capacity and sign-out invalidation. A spawned standalone process prints only the credentials path and closes its own loopback service on quit.
